tagline.text: A farming town in southwestern Cebu with a waterfall, an old church and farm milk

location.label: Location
location.text: Southwestern coast of Cebu Province, about 60–116 km southwest of Cebu City (depending on how the road is measured)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱700–2,000 (per person, a day trip from Cebu City)

children.text: Barili is an agricultural town of 42 barangays lying between the Tañon Strait and the foothills of southwestern mainland Cebu, home to Cebu's tallest waterfall, Mantayupan Falls. Alongside the falls you can enjoy an old church, protected heritage houses, and countryside treats such as farm milk and chicharon.

Barili covers about 122 km² in southwestern mainland Cebu, running from the Tañon Strait inland to the foothills. It borders Aloguinsan to the north, Carcar City and Sibonga to the east, and Dumanjug to the south. As of 2024 it has about 82,000 residents in 42 barangays and is a first-class municipality whose livelihoods are rice and corn fields, poultry and hog raising, cattle, fruit and vegetables. Sources give a distance from Cebu City of about 60–116 km depending on the measure, but it is simplest to assume a bus ride of about 2 hours.

Its history is long. The parish is said to have been founded in 1614 and the town in 1632, and a cross put up by the conquistadors still stands. During the Pacific War, Chief Justice José Abad Santos was captured by Japanese forces here. In 2006 it became the first municipality in Cebu to protect heritage sites by ordinance, so old wooden houses and churches still stand around the town.

For travelers, Barili is a town that makes a satisfying day out of a single waterfall. Mantayupan Falls drops in two stages, with the main inner fall described as about 98 m (Wikipedia says about 61 m, so sources differ) and a small 14 m fall near the entrance. Add the Sta. Ana church in town, the Molave milk station, Barili's chicharon and dairy products, and countryside drives.

Unlike Kawasan Falls or Moalboal, this is not a place thronged with foreigners but a neighborhood spot where Cebuano families come on weekends, so it feels relaxed and simple. Lodging and large tourist facilities are few, so most visitors come on a day trip from Cebu City or combine it with Moalboal. Small fees are charged in many places, so carry plenty of change. The town center has the public market, the bus stop and convenience stores such as 7-Eleven for supplies, and the road to the falls passes rice fields and coconut palms.

Billed as the tallest waterfall on Cebu, it lies in the Campangga valley; past the 14 m fall near the entrance, a hanging bridge leads to the main fall. Locally it is also called Ambakan Falls. For the route and fees, see the
Mantayupan Falls
entry. Many reviewers say the pool in front of the fall is almost empty and quiet early in the day.

Dedicated to the town's patron saint, St. Anne (Sta. Ana), this church is often described as the pride of the townspeople. It is said to have been bombed and burned during the war and then rebuilt. The town fiesta is held around the July 26 feast of St. Anne, so catch it if your dates match.

blocks.title: Heritage houses and a town walk

children.text: Barili is the first municipality in Cebu to start protecting its heritage by ordinance, in 2006. Old wooden houses remain along the town streets, and guides mention names such as the Mancao ancestral house and the Domingo Alcoseba ancestral house. Most are private, so it is polite to look only from the outside.

A shop in Barangay Dakit sells fresh cow and carabao milk, along with ice cream, cheese and yogurt. It is a common cool-down stop on the way back from the falls to town. Milk is best drunk on the spot, and ice cream is welcome in the midday heat. Check the shop's price board.
Restaurants and the public market in town sell chicharon, crispy fried pork skin, cheaply. Snacks such as Shamrock otap are sold near the bus stop, and there is a tilapia restaurant near the falls.

The spring a few minutes from the falls (Boloc-Boloc Spring) is described by some guides as a sulfur-smelling hot spring and by others as fresh spring water. It is good for a light foot or body soak, but facilities are simple, so check on site whether it is open.

On the west coast, Sayaw Beach is described as having white sand and clear water, and small boats can take you to nearby caves and rock formations. Facilities are limited, so bring water and snacks. You reach the beach from town by motorcycle or tricycle, and it is best to ask locally about the exact travel time and fare.

The Panumod Festival, held around the July 26 feast of St. Anne, honors the tradition of taking chickens, cattle and other livestock to market for sale. It began in 2024 in place of the older Kaumahan Festival and has taken part in Cebu's provincial festival Pasigarbo sa Sugbo. Dates and events may change every year.

items.subtitle: The falls and a loop around town

At Mantayupan Falls, take photos, swim or ride the bamboo raft. The earlier you arrive, the quieter it is.
Have lunch near the falls, either tilapia or a packed lunch.
Back in town, walk to Sta. Ana Church and the street of old houses.
Stop at the Molave milk station or the market for chicharon and milk snacks.
Take a bus back to Cebu City. Check the last bus time locally.
This is a day route from Cebu City. Check bus frequency and the last bus locally, and go on a weekday since the falls get crowded on weekends.
Leave Cebu City for Barili. If you hire a vehicle, go to the falls first.
See the falls and have lunch in town.
Go north to Aloguinsan for the Bojo River cruise, or south to Moalboal and rest at your lodging.
If you rely on public transport, it is better to see one place in depth. With a hired vehicle, Aloguinsan or Moalboal fit well after Barili.

The best time for the falls and swimming is the dry season,
December–May
, when the water is clear and the roads are dry. Weekdays are quiet and weekends are busy with local families, so go early in the morning.
In the rainy season,
June–November

, the falls grow fuller, but swollen water in the valley can close them on some days. Rainy days are dangerous, so check the weather forecast. Around July 26 the town is busy with the feast of St. Anne and the Panumod Festival.

Around Barili town and the falls there are a few small lodgings with air-conditioned rooms, but almost no large hotels. Some guides mention about ₱1,000–1,500 per night, but this is not a confirmed recent rate. If you want to stay overnight, it is easier to base yourself in Moalboal to the south and come over.

The food has a strong countryside flavor. Grilled tilapia, chicharon, Shamrock otap (a cookie), and fresh milk, ice cream, cheese and yogurt from the Molave station are typical. At the cottages by the falls entrance you can open a packed lunch or rent a charcoal grill and cook for yourselves.

Barili is also known for livestock trading. According to Wikipedia, the Mantalongon Livestock Market, which draws buyers from southern Cebu and Negros, is linked to the area, and Barangay Guiwanon is known for hand-woven hats made of buri palm leaves. Japitan, on the coast, has a fish port where fresh fish is cheap. These country markets are liveliest in the morning, so plan to see them before lunch.
Go early in the morning, when the falls are quiet and the cliff shade helps your photos.
Small fees are charged separately in several places, such as admission, the raft, the life vest and parking, so carry change.
Many guides say a life vest is required for swimming. Bring a towel, a change of clothes and sandals.
On rainy days the valley swells and the falls may close. Check the forecast before you leave.
Visit Sta. Ana Church quietly and avoid Mass times.
Most heritage houses are private homes, so do not enter without permission.
Bus frequency may thin out, so confirm your return bus in town by 4 PM.
Fees for the falls and transport differ greatly by review. The figures here are approximate, so confirm them locally and avoid swimming in the valley on rainy days.
The pool at the falls is deep. Wear a life vest and do not jump from rocks into murky water.
The hanging bridge sways. Limit the number of people crossing at once and hold children's hands.
After the September 30, 2025 northern Cebu earthquake, repair work continues at some facilities. Check municipal announcements before you go.
The area in front of the falls is very crowded on weekend afternoons. Keep belongings in a waterproof bag and leave valuables behind.
Reviewers say drone signals can be weak in the valley. Check the rules for drone use first.
This is a town with few lodgings and facilities. Bring cash, medicine and a power bank, and return to town before sunset.
